explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase: 99.9% of activation mass, peaking at t=2-4 (85% of mass). It never fires at t=0, on the delimiter, or (apart from about 0.1%) during the copy phase, and is nearly silent from t>=6. It is selective for the current input token in a graded way: y (rate 30%, 26% of mass), then s, j, g, e, r, z, n, b, k. The weakest tokens show up mainly at t=2-4. Precision for y is highest at t=2-3 (about 0.89) and drops at t=1 (0.70) and t>=5 (0.54 at t=5, 0.21 at t=6). It is mostly the first occurrence of the token (93% of mass). Earlier context also modulates it: sequences starting with o/d/u make y at t=3 always fire, while starting with l/t lowers precision. That context is why precision stays near 0.5 and the token+position rule caps F1 at about 0.6. The top activations are y at t=3-4.
